task: Compare Java-generated Rust and source acceptance against the accepted C++ compiler on a bounded standalone ABI-v9 corpus.
observation: Of 52 inputs, C++ accepted 47 and Java accepted 39; Java rejected eight files accepted by C++. None of the 39 pairs that emitted Rust produced byte-identical output. The differential harness captured compiler exit status, error codes, per-file output hashes, and timing in one run; this made it possible to separate Java-only rejection clusters from generated-code differences without compiling or running the generated Rust.
impact: The bounded pass identified open-result inference, enum handling, String method coverage, and runtime/message lowering as focused follow-up areas. The results are limited to the committed Java baseline and do not cover seven uncommitted files on the active Java branch.

resolution.summary: Assessment is complete; L7 review should select any isolated correctness corrections. Semantic equivalence and parity beyond these 52 sources remain unverified.
